_comment: THE IN-LOOP FINISHER DEPLOY MUST LEAVE THE LOOP PAYABLE -- MTG_COMBO_OFF_DEPLOY_TRIAL.
Reconstructed from the user's own reference `claude_s7_gi6`, decision 17 (turn 5); it is the
COMBO OFF sweep's state R-2681076122.
Four mana lands (Adarkar Wastes, Brushland, Conservatory+Fertile Ground, Kitchen+Trace of
Abundance) = six a tap; Eldrazi Displacer's printed {2}{C} (no Training Grounds) and Peregrine
Drake untapping all four: net +3 a pass, 24 iterations sized, TWO Living Wishes in hand.
MTG_COMBO_OFF_EARLY_DEPLOY fires ComboFinishFromHand right after ApplyBlink, i.e. at the exact
moment the ETB untap has put the loop's whole per-iteration income back on the table -- and its
affordability bar there is only 'can I pay the CAST'.  So at k=0 it cast BOTH Living Wishes and
deployed BOTH finishers, nine mana out of the six that had just untapped, and the loop died:
[edf-loop] k=0 post-tapahead  cost={2}{C} float{g2 c2 *2} avail{g2 c2 *2}
[edf-loop] k=1 enter          cost={2}{C} float{}         avail{}
[edf-loop] STOP at k=1: pay-failed
One blink of twenty-four, the opponent on 17, and 49 cards still in their library.
Every cast in the deploy is now trialled on a COPY through the loop's own payer -- pay the cast,
then require the loop's next activation to pay too.  A decline is a DELAY, not a refusal: the
loop banks one more pass at +3 and the next iteration retries.  (And if the board never affords
both, ApplyBlinkLoop's post-loop call passes no keep_payable, so the deploy still happens.)
A/B on this fixture (one binary):
default                          -> 24 blinks, COMBO OFF verified, opponent dead
MTG_COMBO_OFF_DEPLOY_TRIAL=0     -> 1 blink, offered but NOT verified, apply does not win
